title: Compact Cost Table: density variant, accessibility polish, and QA handoff
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Background: The Console cost dashboard currently uses card-based tiles for per-model and per-route spend. Several customers requested a denser, table-style view for high-volume accounts and cost auditors. Goal: deliver a compact density variant of the cost view that preserves the same signals (total spend, change %, sparkline, sample traces) while improving scanability, keyboard navigation, and screen-reader semantics. Scope: deliver a Figma prototype for the compact table variant, accessibility redlines for ARIA and keyboard focus, a final redline PDF for engineering, and QA acceptance criteria. Non-goals: replacing the existing tile layout or analytics backend changes. Decisions and trade-offs: chose a hybrid table-card approach (table rows with expandable detail panels) to keep sparklines and micro-interactions intact while saving vertical height. Opted for a condensed typography stack and tighter token spacing; this increases information density but requires explicit focus states to remain accessible. Chosen sorting defaults: spend desc, then change %. Deliverables: 1) Figma prototype v4 (compact table + row expansion) 2) Redlines + CSS token mapping (pdf) 3) ARIA/keyboard interaction spec 4) QA checklist and known-issues log.
activity_log: 2026-02-20: Ticket created by Maya — initial brief and competitor audit attached.
2026-02-24: Low-fi prototypes reviewed with PM (Ibrahim) — decided to keep row-level expand instead of modal detail to preserve context.
2026-03-02: Accessibility pass completed — added explicit focus ring, skip-to-results anchor, and ARIA labels for sparklines (notes in redlines).
2026-03-04: Stakeholder walkthrough with Sales and Support — agreed to expose a density toggle in Settings and a keyboard shortcut (D) to switch views.
2026-03-06: Visual polish pass (v3) — updated color contrast for the delta chips to meet AA contrast at small text sizes.
2026-03-09: Engineering sync — ENG requested a simplified DOM (avoid nested interactive elements in row) and a data attribute guide for instrumentation (linked in handoff).
2026-03-10: Formal design review scheduled; pushing prototype v4 for sign-off and handoff materials prepared by Arjun.
review_feedback: Ibrahim (PM): Love the density gains; ensure sorting is sticky across sessions — action: add persistence spec.
Leah (QA): Edge case: rows with very long route names should truncate with tooltip; verify tooltip is accessible via keyboard — action: add QA test case.
Sam (Support): Add an on-hover explanation for the delta chip and an audit link to the billing timeline — action: include micro-copy and tracking event names.
Priya (Engineering): DOM concerns for row expansion — prefer CSS-only expand indicator when possible; avoid mounting complex components on hover — action: engineering to propose minimal DOM solution.
Accessibility reviewer (external): Ensure sparklines are conveyed to screen readers as summarized text (e.g., ‘steady up 12%’) — action: add aria-describedby fallback strings.
handoff: Handoff bundle prepared: 1) Figma v4 prototype with redlines frame-by-frame; 2) redline PDF with token-to-CSS mapping (colors, spacing, type); 3) ARIA + keyboard interaction spec document; 4) instrumentation events list (analytics+telemetry); 5) QA checklist. Primary engineering owner: ENG-2899. Key handoff notes: avoid inline buttons inside rows (use row-level menu); use data-cost-row-id attribute for telemetry; implement density toggle as a user preference (persisted via /api/preferences). Link to PR with design assets: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-assets/pull/1282
qa_notes: Acceptance criteria: compact table loads in < 300ms for 200 rows (render only), keyboard-only navigation can open/close row expansion and activate row menu, sparklines have textual summary visible to screen readers, contrast ratios for delta chips >= 4.5:1 for small text.
Test case: truncation — long route name should show ellipsis, tooltip appears on focus and hover, and tooltip text is read by NVDA/VoiceOver.
Test case: density toggle persistence — toggle persists after sign-out and back-in; check via /api/preferences mock.
Test case: instrumentation — row open/close, density toggle, sort change emit events with row id and user_id.
Known issues: sparkline SVGs sometimes lose focus outline in Chromium when wrapped in button; workaround: add explicit focusable wrapper and aria-label for summary.
